headings.text: Choose a tag and sync submodules
Get the first admin invite code

blocks.html:
This is the authoritative procedure for standing up a Deploy App instance on the legacy Docker Compose stack (pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration). On this stack, miniwerk fetches the Let's Encrypt certificates and resolves the per-product subdomains from MW_PRODUCTS, and CFSSL is the internal CA that issues client/service certificates. For the shared in-UI onboarding flow, see Operator quickstart.

Ideally you don't do any of the below manually, but instead use a pipeline & Terraform for deployment. IaC is the way we are doing it.

Required DNS records

All of these must point to your WAN address. When you add more products, follow the same naming pattern — you need a subdomain for every product listed in the composition's miniwerk MW_PRODUCTS variable, plus kc for Keycloak:

Required open ports

Open these (and redirect them to the server if it is behind NAT):

Port Use
80 HTTP
443 HTTPS
8089 TAK
8443 TAK
8446 TAK
9446 Keycloak
4626 Product integration APIs port
4627 ATAK Autoimport ephemeral download port
4666 Battlelog API/UI port
1936 RTMPS (Media MTX video streams)
8322 RTSPS Media MTX video streams)
8890 SRT Media MTX video streams)
9888 HLS Media MTX video streams)
9889 WebRTC Media MTX video streams)
9996 Playback for recorded streams/videos Media MTX video streams)

Clone with submodules

The components are git submodules, so clone recursively. Run all subsequent commands inside the cloned repository.
git clone --recurse-submodules -j8 git@github.com:pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-integration.git

On Windows, do not use git-bash (it breaks Docker containers) — use WSL, and make sure your git client does not rewrite line endings (git config --global core.eol lf, git config --global core.autocrlf false).

Choose a tag and sync submodules

Always a tag so you get a known-good combination of submodules.

Latest tag is a good idea, you can find them at the docker-rasenmaeher-integration tags list.

git tag                              # list available tags
git checkout <TAG_NAME>              # choose a specific tag
git submodule update --init --recursive   # sync submodules to that tag
docker compose build                 # build the matching set

Write the .env file

Create (or make your IaC create) a file named literally .env (not something.env) in the repository root. The canonical example is example_env.sh. Minimal set:

KEYCLOAK_DATABASE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
RM_DATABASE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
POSTGRES_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
LDAP_ADMIN_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
KEYCLOAK_ADMIN_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
TAK_DATABASE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
SYNAPSE_DATABASE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
SYNAPSE_MACAROON_SECRET_KEY="input-secure-password"
SYNAPSE_REGISTRATION_SECRET="input-secure-password"
SERVER_DOMAIN="input-domain"
CFSSL_CA_NAME="input-ca-name"
MW_LE_EMAIL="input-email-for-lets-encrypt"
MW_LE_TEST="false"
TAKSERVER_CERT_PASS="input-secure-password"
TAK_CA_PASS="input-secure-password"
VITE_THEME="${VITE_THEME:-default}"
KEYCLOAK_PROFILEROOT_UUID="input-uuid"
KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_KEY_STORE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
KEYCLOAK_HTTPS_TRUST_STORE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
BL_DATABASE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
RMMTX_DATABASE_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
RMMTX_API_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
RMMTX_SRT_PUB_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
RMMTX_SRT_READ_PASSWORD="input-secure-password"
Replace every input-secure-password with a unique, strong passphrase. Generate UUIDs with:
python -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())'

SERVER_DOMAIN is your domain, MW_LE_EMAIL is the Let's Encrypt contact, and MW_LE_TEST="false" issues real (not staging) certificates. CFSSL_CA_NAME names the internal CA.

Start the services
docker compose up -d

Get the first admin invite code

Generate the first admin invite code from the core API container (rmapi):
docker compose exec -it rmapi /bin/bash -c "rasenmaeher_api addcode"

If you get "no such service -d", the dash you pasted is probably not a real ASCII hyphen (0x2D). When in doubt, type the command by hand instead of copy-pasting.

Then follow the in-UI flow in Operator quickstart to create your admin account, invite users, and approve them.

Service URLs

What URL
Deploy App login page https://domain
Deploy App home page https://mtls.domain
TAK Server Admin UI https://tak.domain:8443/
Keycloak Admin UI https://kc.domain:9443/admin/RASENMAEHER/console/

The TAK OTA update server lives inside the TAK server at <repo>/takserver/update (path depends on where you cloned the repository).

Components (submodules)

The composition is assembled from these submodule repos:

Directory Repo
api pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-api (the core rmapi)
cfssl pvarki/docker-rasenmaeher-cfssl (internal CA)
fpintegration pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-rmfpapi
keycloak pvarki/docker-keycloak
kw_product_init pvarki/golang-kraftwerk-init-helper-cli
openldap pvarki/docker-openldap
miniwerk pvarki/python-rasenmaeher-miniwerk (LE certs, subdomains)
uiv2 pvarki/react-rasenmaeher-ui-v2
takserver pvarki/docker-atak-server
takintegration pvarki/python-tak-rmapi
battlelog pvarki/typescript-liveloki-app
mtxauthz pvarki/python-mediamtx-rmmtxauthz

For updates, lifetime caveats, backups, and the destructive-teardown warning, see Day-2 operations (Docker Compose). To run the stack locally for development (rmlocal / rmdev), see Develop Deploy App.
